sentences.text: Remains include fragments of the skull, the lower jaw, spinal bones, ribs, and the rear swimming fin.
Its braincase is highly primitive, looking more like other diapsids than typical ichthyosaurs.
The rear fin is exceptionally long and thin, containing stretched-out thigh, shin, and ankle bones.
Each spinal bone has two matching hollow spaces at the front, likely helping the animal float.
Unlike many relatives, the bone behind the eye socket does not touch the upper opening in the skull.
The base of the skull features a curved joint surface where the neck connects to the body.
The jaw measures roughly 40 centimeters and holds numerous cone-shaped teeth designed to spear fish.
A specific bone process on the skull is shared with only one other known species of ichthyosaur.
This creature kept ancient skull bones called postparietals that have vanished in all other ichthyosaurs.
Fossils were unearthed in 1965, but the genus was not officially named until 1997 by Sander.
However, the genus name was actually coined earlier by Maisch and Matzke in the year 2000.
To date, the Paleobiology Database lists just a single fossil occurrence for this animal.
The limb arrangement indicates the animal was long but lacked great strength, producing moderate lift.
Phantomosaurus is placed within the larger group known as Cymbospondylidae.
It is formally classified as a member of the family Cymbospondylidae.
This creature is categorized as a reptile.
Fossil evidence places this animal in southern Germany.
